raw_response:
I've been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life — same as my father before me. The soil here is flat, clay-loam, good for grain. I don't overthink it. Everyone in the village grows winter wheat then summer corn on the same fields. That rotation works. The land rests in between, and I can use the same machinery for both. I have about 8 mu of contracted land, and I rent another 4 mu from a neighbor who moved to the city. So 12 mu total.

For wheat, I'll go to the seed station and buy Jimai 22 — it's what I've used the last few years, stable yield, the county tech station pushed it. I won't try something new at my age. Planting in mid-October, I'll rotary till first, then apply compound fertilizer in the base, and follow up with urea at jointing. I irrigate at least three times for wheat — before winter, at jointing, and at heading. If it looks dry at grain fill I add one more. I've seen what happens when you skip the jointing irrigation. Not worth it.

For corn, I plant right after wheat harvest in June. I use Xianyu 335 hybrid — the yields are solid and I can buy it locally. I do rotary till lightly after wheat, then direct seed. One base fertilizer application, one top-dress when the corn is knee-high. Corn here gets rain in summer so maybe one irrigation unless July is bad.

Pesticides: wheat gets herbicide in spring, one fungicide spray before heading for powdery mildew. Corn gets herbicide right after planting, and I spray for corn borer if I see damage.
